claim_being_audited: That certifying the model is compliant because aggregate performance exceeds the deployment threshold, while the small-business support slice weakness can be handled through explicit disclosure since no approved mitigation is in the admissible record.
specific_concerns: The audit relies only on the Actor's summary of evidence rather than the underlying admissible evidence.
The claimed numeric thresholds and deltas are not independently verifiable from the record available to this role.
The packet asserts the slice weakness is material enough to require disclosure, but the underlying materiality basis is not shown directly.
The conclusion depends on certification being disclosure-based, but there is no direct evidence that the actual certification packet contains the required disclosure.
The absence of an approved mitigation is asserted, but the auditor cannot independently confirm the approval record from the available evidence.
unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is exactly 1.1 percentage points below warning and 2.6 points below preferred threshold.
There is no approved mitigation in the admissible record.
Certification is supportable in this specific case because the required disclosure is or will be included in the certification packet.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BMCARD-025-A through BMCARD-025-E, not just their identifiers.
Provide the exact evaluation table showing aggregate and small-business support slice results, thresholds, and sample sizes.
Provide the policy excerpt or decision memo establishing whether this slice weakness is classified as material in this case.
Provide the actual certification/model-card text showing the weakness is explicitly disclosed.
Provide the approval log or governance record confirming that no mitigation has been approved.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty can weaken confidence in magnitude estimates but does not by itself resolve an unresolved subgroup weakness.
A compliant certification decision must be supported by admissible evidence showing both the performance facts and the presence of required disclosure or approved mitigation.
